To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
anisotropically reinforced composites are expected to have better creep resistance than isotropic ones.
the anisotropic disc following Hill criterion has lower tangential strain rate and the compressive radial strain is also lowered.
the anisotropic disc following Hill yield criteria is less prone to creep as compared to the isotropic disc.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the steady state creep behaviour in the orthotropic composite disc using Hill yield criterion of plasticity.
the analysis of steady state creep behaviour of a disc made of an orthotropic material.
creep analysis of an orthotropic disc made of a composite containing SiC whisker reinforcement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of anisotropy in composites containing whisker reinforcement is helpful in reducing the creep rate and the anisotropically reinforced composite is a more desirable engineering material than the isotropic composite.
anisotropies help in reducing the creep rate in both tangential and radial directions.
anisotropically reinforced disc would be more creep resistant as compared to an isotropic one, following von Mises yield condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anisotropies in composites containing whisker and short fibers are not always detrimental and in some cases they may be beneficial.
the anisotropic material following Hill yield criterion is better in resisting creep deformation than the isotropic material following von Mises yield criteria.
the anisotropic behaviour of the composite material is a consequence of the processing of the composite material and it helps in reducing the creep response in the composite material.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the anisotropic creep analysis in the rotating disc made of orthotropic material can be carried out by using the Hill yield criterion and the anisotropic constants can be taken from the experimental data.
the creep in the disc following von Misse criterion is more dangerous as compared to the creep in the orthotropic discs following Hill yield criterion.
the anisotropic creep analysis of rotating disc is a useful tool to predict the creep life of rotating disc made of an orthotropic composite.
